guards.what: Fabricator._spawn_bot draws its bot class from the SHARED combat rng; Fabricator.cs:115 draws from RunRng.MonsterAi
guards.issue: Fabricator.cs:115 is `base.RunRng.MonsterAi.NextItem(items)` -- the dedicated MonsterAi stream, the same stream MonsterModel.RollMove names. fabricator.py:176 is `ctx.hooks.combat._rng.choice(choices)` -- the SHARED legacy combat random.Random. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b07.py spawn-rng`): in a legacy CombatRng the two are the same object (`combat._rng is combat_rng.monster_ai -> True`), but in a parity CombatRng (CombatRng.parity, combat_rng.py:41-46) monster_ai is a GameRandomAdapter over a separate RunRngSet stream, so they are DIFFERENT streams; one _spawn_bot burns 2 shared-rng draws (the class choice plus the spawn's HP roll) and 0 MonsterAi draws, where the game burns exactly 1 MonsterAi draw for the choice (Rng.NextItem -> NextInt(0, count), Rng.cs:255-266) and 0 shared draws. Observable: a different bot is summoned and both streams' counters desynchronise for the rest of the run. This is the SAME BUG CLASS as monster_state_machine G6 but a DIFFERENT site -- G6 is powers.py:2233's roll_move; this is a content-level NextItem the seam's `move-rng` probe cannot see because it only scans roll_move call sites. Not re-verdicting G6. LIVE (rule 6): 'fabricator' is in Glory's normal_keys (rooms.py:189) so FABRICATOR_NORMAL is reachable, the spawn path runs on the Fabricator's first move (executed: `spawn-content`), and the parity CombatRng is the shipped conformance-runner mode.

guards.what: CanFabricate (Fabricator.cs:51) vs Fabricator._alive_count / _can_fabricate (fabricator.py:136-146), including the opening roll's missing enemies list
guards.rationale: C#: `CombatState.GetTeammatesOf(Creature).Count(c => c.IsAlive) < 4`. GetTeammatesOf returns GetCreaturesOnSide(creature.Side) and its own doc comment says it INCLUDES the creature itself (CombatState.cs:394-400), so the threshold counts the Fabricator plus its live bots -- the sim's `sum(1 for c in combat.enemies if not c.is_gone) < 4` is the same population and the same threshold. `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:43-46), and nothing in this encounter escapes, so it equals `!IsAlive` here; the sim's enemies list retains corpses where C#'s Enemies does not, which is exactly why the filter is needed. The interesting part is the OPENING roll: unlike every other unit in this batch the Fabricator's initial state is the ConditionalBranchState, so monster_state_machine step 30's sticky early return does NOT fire and the first roll really walks the branch. Executed (`monster_probes_b07.py fab-open`): `initial state: fabricateBranch  is MoveState -> False`, `opening move rolled: FABRICATE_MOVE`, `state_log after construction: ['FABRICATE_MOVE']`. At that moment combat.enemies has not been assigned (combat.py:134 is still evaluating its right-hand side), so _alive_count takes its documented fallback and returns 1 -- which is the TRUE count, because FabricatorNormal.GenerateMonsters yields exactly one monster (FabricatorNormal.cs:44-47) and it is the game's only Fabricator encounter (`grep -rln Fabricator src/Core/Models/Encounters/` returns FabricatorNormal.cs alone). Both sides therefore compute 1 < 4 and draw one branch roll. The fallback would diverge only in a multi-monster Fabricator encounter, which exists in neither tree.

ConditionalBranchState.GetNextState returns the FIRST branch whose Evaluate() > 0 and THROWS if none match (ConditionalBranchState.cs:44-54); the sim is identical including the raise (state_machine.py:228-232). Add order is therefore observable, and it matches: executed (`monster_probes_b07.py branch-order`) `Fabricator.fabricateBranch: first-true-wins order ['RAND', 'DISINTEGRATE_MOVE']` vs C#'s AddState(randomBranchState, () => CanFabricate) then AddState(moveState3, () => !CanFabricate). The two conditions are exact complements on both sides, so the throw arm is unreachable on both.

guards.what: what the spawn actually produces: which bot, the _lastSpawned filter, MinionPower, and list position
guards.rationale: Fabricator.cs:110-118: `options.Where(m => m != _lastSpawned)`, one _lastSpawned field SHARED between the defensive and aggressive pools, then MinionPower 1 with the Fabricator as applier. fabricator.py:171-182 reproduces all of it: one `self._last_spawned` field, the same filter, `PowerCmd.apply(..., MinionPower, 1, applier=self)`. Pool membership and ORDER match -- C#'s HashSets are {Zapbot, Stabbot} (aggro, Fabricator.cs:25-29) and {Guardbot, Noisebot} (defense, :31-35), the sim's lists are [Zapbot, Stabbot] and [Guardbot, Noisebot] (fabricator.py:115-116). FabricateMove spawns defensive THEN aggressive (Fabricator.cs:79-80 vs fabricator.py:185-186); FabricatingStrikeMove attacks then spawns one aggressive bot (:89 vs :190). Executed (`monster_probes_b07.py spawn-content`, seeds 0-3): the shared _lastSpawned makes two consecutive aggressive spawns always differ (`['Fabricator','Guardbot','Zapbot','Stabbot','Zapbot']` at seed 0), every spawn carries `minion`, and net_ids run 1..5 in attach order. The DEATH-vs-REMOVAL trap does not bite here: the sim never removes a dead bot from combat.enemies, and the C# side only ever reads the pool through _lastSpawned, never through the enemy list.

guards.what: Encounter.GetNextSlot placement (Fabricator.cs:115) has no sim analogue
guards.rationale: Presentation only, per SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 (monster stream) and monster_state_machine guards N2/N5. FabricatorNormal.Slots is [bot1, bot2, fabricator, bot3, bot4] and GetNextSlot returns the first entry no live enemy occupies (EncounterModel.cs:245-248), so bots visually fill around the Fabricator. It is NOT a list-order mechanism: CombatState.AddCreature appends to _enemies regardless of the slot (CombatState.cs:534-547), which is what the sim's `combat.enemies.append` (cmds.py:262-265) reproduces. GetNextSlot's mechanical use elsewhere -- TwoTailedRat.cs:204 gating a summon on the slots being full -- is not used by the Fabricator, which gates on CanFabricate instead, and the two gates coincide (max 4 bots = 4 bot slots).

IsLiveCombat() is `return true` on the real CombatState (CombatState.cs:608-611) and `return false` on NullCombatState (NullCombatState.cs:146-149), i.e. it is exactly the 'am I attached to a real combat' predicate the sim spells as `combat is None`. NullCombatState.cs is cited by NAME only and is not hashed.
